submission.justification: Module-D2 gives the most light (38 PE/MeV at 20% coverage), but 30% of D2 modules failed in thermal cycling because the light-guide bonding cracks on cooldown. That breaks the hard limit of at most 5% failures, so D2 is ruled out. Of the two designs that pass, D3 (2% failures) gives more light than D1 (0.5% failures): 27 vs 18 PE/MeV at 20% coverage. Light collection rises with coverage, so I chose the 30% maximum. Feedthroughs are confirmed for up to 30%. Scaling the 2025 summary's approximate coverage^0.8 relation, D3 at 30% gives an estimated 37 PE/MeV. No new simulation was run (I had no simulation tool), so this number is an extrapolation and not a fresh result. The failure rates come from a 40-module batch per design, which is a small sample.

requirements.evidence: D3 gives the most light of the designs that pass thermal cycling: 27 PE/MeV at 20% coverage, about 37 PE/MeV at 30% (extrapolated using coverage^0.8 from the 2025 simulation summary, not re-simulated).

requirements.requirement: Module must be one of the three designs in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Module-D3 (wavelength-shifting bar with SiPM readout) is listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: At most 5% failures after 20 thermal cycles (300 K to 87 K)
requirements.evidence: thermal_cycling_tests.md: D3 had 2% failures in a 40-module batch (D2 had 30%, so it is excluded).
30% is within range, and the 2026-01-20 meeting notes confirm enough feedthroughs for up to 30%.

requirements.requirement: Submit one module design and coverage
